title: Temperature scales: Celsius, Kelvin and Fahrenheit (তাপমাত্রার স্কেল)
placement: Book pages 163–164, topic 6.2 (পদার্থের তাপমাত্রিক ধর্ম): in place of চিত্র ৬.০২ (সেলসিয়াস, কেলভিন এবং ফারেনহাইট তাপমাত্রার স্কেল), next to the paragraphs on the Celsius and Kelvin scales, absolute zero and the triple point of water.
description: Figure 6.02 of the book (pages 163–164, topic 6.2) brought to life: three glass thermometers side by side on a pale blue board standing on a bench, the Celsius, the Kelvin and the Fahrenheit one, each with its own graduations and a dark mercury column that rises to the same height in all three. Lines run across at the fixed points as in the book (0 °C = 273.15 K = 32 °F and 100 °C = 373.15 K = 212 °F) and a crimson line marks the temperature now. One big button walks through the book's own temperatures in the book's order: melting ice, boiling water, a room at 30 °C (30 + 273.15 = 303.15 K), absolute zero (the tubes then show the whole way down to -273.15 °C = 0 K) and the triple point of water (0.01 °C = 273.16 K); a drag on the mercury sets any other temperature (whole degrees, never below absolute zero). The panel shows the three readings, T_K = T_C + 273.15 with the student's numbers, 'saying 10 °C rose is the same as saying 10 K rose' as soon as the mercury has moved, and the rule in the book's words (thermometric property and substance, the fixed points, absolute zero, the triple point). Test tab: 5 questions (Celsius to Kelvin, Kelvin to Celsius, a rise in K, absolute zero in °C, boiling or melting in °F), every wrong choice a real mistake with its own note. Phone-first, Bangla and English.
